overview: TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System) is an RBI-regulated digital platform that enables MSMEs to unlock working capital by converting their approved receivables into immediate cash through competitive bidding by financiers. RXIL (Receivables Exchange of India Limited), established in December 2014 as a joint venture of SIDBI and NSE, is India's first TReDS platform. It facilitates invoice discounting without collateral or debt, providing funds within 24 hours of invoice approval, and supports MSME liquidity by bridging the payment gap between buyers and sellers.
objectives: Facilitate MSMEs to unlock working capital by converting receivables into cash
Provide capital access to credit-starved small businesses in India
Enable competitive discount rates through auction mechanism among multiple financiers
Ensure end-to-end digital, paperless, and transparent processes
Facilitate seamless data flow between participants and the platform
Support priority sector lending benefits for funds disbursed through the platform
Minimize risk of default by anchoring credit calls on buyer repayment ability
Provide access to quality customers for financiers at minimal cost
eligibility: MSMEs engaged for at least 1 year since registration can register on TReDS. Eligibility factors include: GST compliance history, business turnover, buyer credit profile, invoice age, payment history, financial stability. A strong buyer profile often improves financing approval chances. MSMEs must be classified as per the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 (MSMED Act).
benefits: Faster access to working capital (funds within 24 hours), reduced payment delays, lower borrowing costs compared to loans, no added debt on books, competitive bidding in auction models, seamless digital experience, ERP integration, enhanced procurement terms, strengthened supplier relationships, quicker payments, access to multiple financiers, without recourse borrowing, lower cost of funds, priority sector lending benefits, low risk of default, access to quality customers, automated reconciliation.
financial_support: Funds are disbursed through competitive bidding by multiple authorised banks and NBFCs on approved invoices. MSMEs receive early payment based on the best bid, often within 24 hours, while repayment responsibility rests with the corporate buyer on the invoice due date. The mechanism allows MSMEs to convert receivables into working capital without taking on traditional short-term debt or providing collateral. RXIL has facilitated invoice financing exceeding ₹2 lakh crore, with over 51,500 MSMEs registered across 1,160+ cities and participation from 70+ banks and NBFCs.

caveats: MSMEs must be engaged in business for at least 1 year since registration
Only tax invoices are accepted as valid instruments for financing
The counterparty (buyer/seller) must provide acceptance of the invoice on the TReDS platform
Financing of factoring units is not guaranteed and depends on financier bids and cost bearer acceptance
If no bids are received from financiers, the invoice is settled outside the TReDS platform
A Factoring Unit may be withdrawn from the TReDS portal only if the bid is not accepted by the cost bearer
Transaction charges (incl. applicable service tax) are to be paid by the charge bearer to RXIL for factoring
